anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — The spec covers the download, empty-header and 10000-row rows, but it hands the column-order row (a widgets acceptance criterion) to mailer, so nothing in widgets is required to emit id, name, status.
findings:
- [blocker] scope @ "The CSV contains id, name, and status columns in that order. - elsewhere: acme/mailer" and Design "Column selection is assigned to mailer" — The ticket lists this row under `### acme/widgets`. Mailer only sends the email and has no control over the CSV body that GET /widgets/export.csv produces. This also contradicts Goal "This change delivers all four widgets rows" and Verification "Request tests check ... column order". → Mark the row `in-scope`. Replace the Design sentence with "The header row is exactly `id,name,status` and each data row emits those fields in that order." — probed: none
- [major] gap @ Design "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000" — The problem says users download *their* widgets, but the spec gives no ownership or tenant filter and no authorization check. As written, the endpoint could export every widget in the system. → Add "Scope the query to widgets owned by the current user, or the user's account. Unauthenticated requests get 401/redirect." Add a request test proving that other users' widgets are excluded. — probed: none
- [major] ambiguity @ Design "write the header even when no rows exist" — The header's contents are never defined, so neither "exports only the header" nor column order can be tested from the Design alone. → State the literal header line and the per-field serialization: status as its stored string, name as-is. Also state the line terminator (CRLF vs LF). — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification "CSV escaping" — Escaping is tested but never specified in Design. → Add "Fields containing comma, quote, CR or LF are quoted per RFC 4180, with embedded quotes doubled." — probed: none
- [minor] oversimplification @ Design "in batches of 1000" — The spec does not say whether the response is streamed or buffered. With 10000 rows this matters for memory and time-to-first-byte, and for what "complete response" measures. → State whether the response streams batch-by-batch or is built fully before sending. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope" — The row is already marked in-scope, so the conditional is dead wording. The benchmark environment and the pass threshold are also unstated. → Change to "Run the 10000-widget benchmark. It passes if request start to the last byte is under 60s on <named environment>." — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut
